summary.name: Webmail
summary.one_liner: Webmail is email accessed through a standard web browser rather than a dedicated desktop email client, and this Wikipedia article covers its history, deployment, rendering issues, and privacy concerns.
keywords: cc:mail for the world wide web
use_cases: comparing webmail with desktop email clients
checking POP3 vs IMAP behaviour with webmail
summary.what_it_does: The article defines webmail as email service accessed via a web browser, contrasted with desktop email client software. It traces early webmail implementations from 1993 to 1995, including CERN, Lotus cc:Mail, and several European and US projects, and notes the spread of webmail through ISPs, hosting providers, and free services like Hotmail and RocketMail in 1996. It explains how POP3 and IMAP usage affects message availability between webmail and desktop clients. It also covers privacy concerns such as ad-targeted content analysis and the risk of unencrypted HTTP access, noting HTTPS adoption by Gmail and Yahoo! Mail.
notable: Covers early webmail history from CERN in 1993 and 1995 implementations such as Lotus cc:Mail and Webex
Explains POP3 vs IMAP effects on webmail and desktop client consistency
Documents privacy issues including ad-targeted scanning and the move to HTTPS-only by Gmail and Yahoo! Mail
caveats: Describes webmail in general; it is not a single installable product
Page is encyclopedia history and does not list current webmail software to install
